purpose: How a public name or behaviour leaves the Framework. One version line stays long; legacy leaves on a calendar, not on a version number.

stages.compat: Still works through an alias or a shim, recorded in contracts/changes/journal.json, noted at runtime in SF.deprecations (and in the console when the page opts in). Documented with its replacement.
stages.removed: The code is gone. The journal record stays forever as a tombstone, so any older consumer can still be upgraded by reading it.

remove_after_rule: The first sweep day on or after deprecated_on + compat_days.

extension.requires: a reason naming the consumer that still depends on the name and the date it migrates

sweep: On each sweep day every compat record whose remove_after has passed is removed: known consumers are scanned with scripts/sf-upgrade.mjs first, the code and its alias go, the record becomes removed with removed_on, and the gate holds it. A sweep that cannot finish by its day is extended before the day, never after: the gate must not be red on a day the work is in hand, or a known red teaches everyone to read past it. Only the sweeper edits the journal; anyone else who meets a due record says so and waits.
